texts.core.kirchhoff.equations.current_sources: {p} and {q} are in series: two current sources set the same current.
texts.core.kirchhoff.equivalent.delta: {names} form a delta: each lies between two of the same three nodes, and neither series nor parallel applies. Turned into a star around a new node, each corner gets the product of the two resistors at it over the sum of all three.
texts.core.kirchhoff.equivalent.neither_series: The rest of the network is neither in series nor in parallel, so it is solved with the node rule: a test current I = 1 A flows in at A and out at B, and B is at 0 V.

texts.core.kirchhoff.equivalent.parallel: {names} are in parallel: they lie between the same two nodes.
texts.core.kirchhoff.equivalent.series: {pn} and {qn} are in series: nothing else branches off between them, so the same current flows through both.
texts.core.kirchhoff.equivalent.shorted: A and B are joined by a wire, so no current flows through the resistors.
texts.core.kirchhoff.equivalent.shorted_part: {id} is shorted: both of its terminals are on the same node.
texts.core.kirchhoff.equivalent.star: {names} form a star: they meet at a node where nothing else is connected, and neither series nor parallel applies. Turned into a delta between their outer ends, each side gets the sum of the products of two arms over the arm opposite it.

texts.core.logic.step.maxterms: Each row with 0 gives a maxterm: the OR of every variable, negated where the row has a 1.
texts.core.logic.step.minterms: Each row with 1 gives a minterm: the AND of every variable, negated where the row has a 0.
texts.core.logic.step.nand_de_morgan: Double negation, then De Morgan: the OR of the products becomes a NAND of the products' NANDs:
texts.core.logic.step.nand_form_rewrite: The {gate} form gate by gate (gates: {gates}, gate inputs: {inputs}, levels: {levels}):
texts.core.logic.step.nand_gates: The gates, each over the inputs and the earlier gates, with its level:
texts.core.logic.step.nand_inverters: Each negated variable from a {gate} with both inputs tied, one per variable:
texts.core.logic.step.nand_rewrite: Gate by gate: each NOT an inverter, each AND a NAND and an inverter, each OR a NAND of the inverted inputs, each XOR four NANDs:
texts.core.logic.step.nand_single: A term of one literal needs no {gate} of its own; it goes negated straight into the output {gate}:
texts.core.logic.step.nand_split: With only 2-input gates, a {gate} of {m} inputs becomes a balanced tree of {count} gates:
texts.core.logic.step.nor_de_morgan: Double negation, then De Morgan: the AND of the sums becomes a NOR of the sums' NORs:
texts.core.logic.step.nor_rewrite: Gate by gate: each NOT an inverter, each OR a NOR and an inverter, each AND a NOR of the inverted inputs, each XNOR four NORs:
texts.core.logic.step.ones: The rows that are 1 give the minterms of {output}:
texts.core.logic.step.petrick_bound: The products dearer than a cover found greedily ({terms} terms, {literals} literals) are dropped.
texts.core.logic.step.petrick_step: Multiplied by the next sum, with absorption:
texts.core.logic.step.petrick_sums: Petrick's method: each column left needs one of the prime implicants over it.
texts.core.logic.step.primes: The prime implicants, the terms that never combined:

texts.core.logic.step.qm_minterms: The rows that are 1 or don't care (in brackets), grouped by their number of 1s; ✓ marks a term that combines with one of the next group:
texts.core.logic.step.qm_not_combined: These pairs of neighbouring groups with the same dashes differ in more than one place and do not combine:
